_comment_GENERATION_INSTRUCTIONS: GENERATION INSTRUCTIONS (AI reads this; remove _comment blocks from output)
MANDATORY STRUCTURE — Every collection MUST have these folders (skip only if N/A):
📁 01 – Setup / Prerequisites
• Create ALL config/data needed by subsequent requests
• Verify setup succeeded (GET after POST)
• Sync IDs: if resources might already exist, have a 'sync' request that
extracts IDs from existing data (handle 409 Conflict gracefully)
• Test scripts MUST set environment variables for chaining
📁 02 – CRUD Operations (admin/management API if exists)
• One request per HTTP method per resource
• GET single + GET list (paginated if applicable)
• POST create (with full valid body)
• PUT/PATCH update (partial update if supported)
• DELETE (if the API supports it)
• Auth failure cases: missing key → 401, wrong key → 401/403
📁 03 – Happy Path (primary feature use case)
• The MAIN use case that this feature enables
• Verify: status code + response shape + key field values
• If feature has chaining (request A → extract → use in B), show full chain
• Verify custom response headers if the feature adds them
📁 04 – Bulk / Batch Operations (if applicable)
• Small batch (5 items) — baseline
• Medium batch (20 items) — normal load
• Large batch (near-limit) — stress boundary
• Verify batch response format and per-item status
📁 05 – Edge Cases & Limits
• Boundary values: 0, 1, max, max+1
• Rate limits / quotas exceeded (if applicable)
• Resource not found → 404
• Resource already exists → 409 Conflict
• Concurrent access scenarios (document as manual test)
📁 06 – Validation Errors
• One request per required field (missing each one individually)
• Invalid format for each typed field (wrong type, too long, etc.)
• Invalid enum values
• Malformed JSON body
• Empty body where body is required
• Test scripts verify: status 400 + specific error code/message
📁 07 – Authentication & Authorization
• Missing auth header → 401
• Invalid/expired token → 401
• Wrong role/scope → 403 (if RBAC exists)
• Valid auth with minimal permissions → verify access
📁 08 – Failure Scenarios
• Downstream service unavailable (document: manual or mock)
• Feature disabled via config → expected response
• Database unavailable (document: manual)
• Any FAIL_OPEN / FAIL_CLOSED behavior
📁 09 – Monitoring & Status (if admin/status endpoints exist)
• Health check endpoint
• Feature-specific status (bucket status, cache state, etc.)
• Metrics endpoint (if exposed)
📁 10 – Teardown / Cleanup
• DELETE all test data created in folder 01
• Reset any state (caches, buckets, queues)
• Verify cleanup succeeded
PRE-REQUEST SCRIPT (collection-level) — MANDATORY:
Every collection MUST have a collection-level pre-request script that:
1. Resolves base_url from active_env variable
2. Auto-switches API keys based on active_env (<env>_<key> pattern)
3. Generates any dynamic values (timestamps, UUIDs, test emails)
TEST SCRIPTS — MANDATORY on EVERY request:
Every request MUST have test scripts that verify:
1. Status code (exact expected code, not just 2xx)
2. Response shape (required fields exist with correct types)
3. Value assertions (for known/expected values)
4. Variable extraction (set env vars for chaining to next request)
For error cases:
2. Error response structure (errorCode, message, details)
3. Specific error code value (not just 'has errorCode')
QUALITY STANDARDS (non-negotiable):
• NO hardcoded URLs — all use {{base_url}} resolved from active_env
• NO hardcoded API keys — all use {{variable}} from environment
• NO assumed field names — grep DTO classes for exact field names
• NO assumed error codes — grep exception handlers for exact codes
• NO empty test scripts — every request has assertions
• NO orphan variables — every {{var}} must be defined in env or set by script
• Collection MUST be runnable sequentially (01 → 02 → ... → 10)
• Test scripts handle idempotency (201 OR 409 for create requests)
• All folder descriptions explain what the folder covers
• Collection description lists all required environment variables
ACCURACY (grep everything):
Before generating ANY request, grep for:
• Endpoint path: @RequestMapping, @GetMapping, @PostMapping annotations
OR: Express routes, FastAPI decorators, Go handler registrations,
proto service definitions, schema.graphql Query/Mutation types
• Request body: DTO class fields (including @NotNull, @Valid, @Size etc.)
OR: TypeScript interfaces, Python Pydantic models, Go structs, proto messages
• Response body: ResponseEntity generic type or return DTO
OR: return type annotations, response schemas, proto response messages
• Error responses: @ControllerAdvice, @ExceptionHandler, error codes
OR: error middleware, exception handlers, custom error types
• Auth headers: security filter chain, interceptors, @PreAuthorize
OR: passport strategies, auth middleware, guard decorators
• Valid values: enum classes, @Pattern annotations, validators
OR: zod schemas, marshmallow validators, validation middleware
DO NOT invent field names, paths, or error codes. Every value in the
collection must be traceable to a grep result in the source code.
ADVANCED PATTERNS (include when detected):
FILE UPLOAD (multipart/form-data):
• Use Postman's body type 'formdata' with file fields
• Test: valid file → 200/201, empty file → 400, oversized → 413, wrong type → 415
• Include content-type negotiation tests
PAGINATION (offset/cursor-based):
• First page → extract cursor/next link
• Next page (using extracted cursor) → verify continuity
• Empty page (past end) → verify empty result set
• Invalid cursor → 400
• Page size limits: 0, 1, max, max+1
ASYNC / LONG-RUNNING OPERATIONS:
• Submit job → 202 Accepted + Location/job-id
• Poll status → 200 with status: 'processing'
• Poll until complete → 200 with status: 'completed' + result
• Cancel in-progress → 200/204
• Get expired/non-existent job → 404/410
GRAPHQL (if detected — use POST to /graphql):
• Separate folder for: queries, mutations, subscriptions
• Each request body: { query: '...', variables: {...} }
• Test scripts check data field + errors array
• Validation: malformed query → errors, missing variable → errors
WEBSOCKET / SSE (document-only — cannot automate in Postman):
• Document connection URL and headers in folder description
• Document expected message sequence
• Add a REST endpoint test that triggers the WS/SSE event (if exists)
• Mark as 'MANUAL TEST — see description for WebSocket/SSE test procedure'
IDEMPOTENCY KEYS (if API supports them):
• Same key + same body → same response (no duplicate creation)
• Same key + different body → 409 or 422
• Expired key → treated as new request
